'''''Macaranga''''' is a large [[genus]] of [[Old World]] [[tropical]] trees of the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Euphorbiaceae]] and the only genus in the [[subtribe]] '''Macaranginae''' (tribe [[Acalypheae]]). Native to Africa, [[Australasia]], Asia and various islands of the Indian and Pacific Oceans, the genus comprises over 300 different [[species]].<ref name=POWO/><ref>Govaerts, R., Frodin, D.G. & Radcliffe-Smith, A. (2000). World Checklist and Bibliography of Euphorbiaceae (and Pandaceae) 1-4: 1-1622. The Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew.</ref> It was first described as a genus in 1806, based on specimens collected on the Island of [[Mauritius]].<ref name=i/><ref name=j>[http://www.tropicos.org/Name/40010815 Tropicos, genus ''Macaranga'']</ref> Many species, such as ''[[Macaranga gigantea]]'' have uncommonly large leaves, and many are [[peltate]].

''Macaranga'' are noted for being [[pioneer species]]. ''Macaranga'' species are used as food plants by the [[larva]]e of some [[Lepidoptera]] species including ''[[Endoclita|Endoclita malabaricus]]''. ''Macaranga'' species often form symbioses with ant ([[Formicidae]]) species (particularly ''[[Crematogaster]]'' ants of the subgenus ''[[Decacrema]]'') because they have hollow stems that can serve as nesting space and occasionally provide nectar. The trees benefit because the ants attack herbivorous insects and either drive them away or feed on them.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1007/s000400050064 |title=The two-partner ant-plant system of ''Camponotus (Colobopsis)'' sp. 1 and ''Macaranga puncticulata'' (Euphorbiaceae): Natural history of the exceptional ant partner |year=1998 |last1=Federle |first1=W. |last2=Maschwitz |first2=U. |last3=Fiala |first3=B. |journal=Insectes Sociaux |volume=45 |issue=1 |pages=1–16|s2cid=26704950 }}</ref>

==Uses==
* Macaranga gum, a crimson [[resin]], is obtained from ''[[Macaranga indica]]''.
* ''[[Macaranga tanarius]]'' leaves are used by the [[Rungus language|Rungus]] indigenous people in [[Sabah]], [[Malaysia]] to pack cooked rice into bundles to preserve it and impart a pleasant aroma.<ref>https://www.facebook.com/pg/geraioa/photos/?tab=album&album_id=10157033718332367 {{User-generated source|certain=yes|date=March 2022}}</ref>
